nodes.label: Config folder (Sword, Items)
nodes.rationale: Shared tuning tables replicated to clients so UI can show the same numbers the server uses for damage and item definitions.

nodes.label: Boulder decor set (5 Models)
nodes.rationale: Code-generated rocks, 3-5 Anchored Ball parts each. Scenery only.

nodes.label: Tree decor set (10 Models)
nodes.rationale: Code-generated foliage: each tree is a Cylinder trunk plus 3 Ball canopy parts, all Anchored. Scenery only — no script references them.

nodes.label: Voxel Terrain
nodes.rationale: The actual playable ground. EnemyCombat raycasts against it so spawned rigs snap to the surface instead of spawning buried or floating; this is why the Baseplate can sit unused 80 studs below.

nodes.label: Baseplate
nodes.rationale: 2048x16x2048 at y=-80, fully transparent — the visible ground is Terrain, not this. Acts as a fallback floor far below the playable surface.

nodes.label: Runtime-spawned enemy rigs
nodes.rationale: Enemies exist only at runtime: EnemyCombat builds R6 rigs from scratch with Motor6D joints and parents them to Workspace. Nothing enemy-shaped is saved in the place file, so the world export cannot show them. Four archetypes: Grunt, Scout, Brute, and the Boss (Iron Warlord) — the Boss is scale 1.5 and is the only one built with a welded sword and a swingWeapon() shoulder animation.

nodes.label: Lemonade RPG place (root)
nodes.rationale: Sword-combat RPG built by the Lemonade AI Studio plugin; every instance it touched carries a _lemonadeUniqueId attribute. 186 instances total across 9 services, 28 Luau scripts.

nodes.label: RemoteEvents folder
nodes.rationale: The entire client/server contract of the game: 14 RemoteEvents, every one of them the only channel between a server system and its matching client UI. No RemoteFunctions — everything is fire-and-forget.

nodes.label: WeaponSmith NPC (Model)
nodes.rationale: Static R6 noob rig placed at (12, 3, 8). It is the game's only shop-style interaction point: clicking it opens the gold-for-damage weapon upgrade flow. Purely decorative otherwise — it has a Humanoid but no AI script drives it.

nodes.label: WeaponSmith ClickDetector
nodes.rationale: MaxActivationDistance 32. The single entry point into the upgrade UI.

nodes.label: WeaponSmith Dialog (unused)
nodes.rationale: Leftover Roblox sample dialog ('This is the dialog system!'). No script reads it; the real interaction is the ClickDetector. Dead content.

nodes.label: ClassicSword (Tool)
nodes.rationale: Doubles as the starter weapon AND the template SwordDropSystem clones for every rarity drop — the clone is retinted per rarity and given DamageMult and Rarity attributes.

nodes.label: ClassicSword Handle
nodes.rationale: Carries the sword mesh and all three sounds. SwordDropSystem recolors this part to Neon in the rarity colour when it clones the tool.

nodes.label: SwordLunge sound (unused)
nodes.rationale: Present on the Handle but never played by any script — leftover from the stock Roblox classic sword.
